longForm.heroHook: Draws material into the probe, then shears it apart. No cavitation, no ultrasonic complexity.
longForm.heroLead: Rotor-stator homogenization works on a different principle than ultrasonic probes entirely: material gets drawn directly into the generator probe and exposed to intense mechanical and hydraulic shear as it passes through, not broken apart by cavitation bubbles. A 144W high-torque motor drives speeds from 5,000 to 35,000 rpm, processing 0.03mL to 500mL samples (up to 1L depending on probe and viscosity) through the PRO Quick Connect stainless-steel probe system. New thumb-operated speed control and a redesigned ergonomic housing keep operation one-handed, while the quick-connect system delivers secure coupling, reduced vibration, and easy cleaning every time a probe swaps out. Existing PRO Quick Connect probes stay compatible with this redesigned motor unit, so current ProScientific users can upgrade without replacing probes or accessories already on hand.

sections.description: Bio-Gen PRO200 homogenizer product information: rotor-stator mechanism, probe system, and configuration options.
body: High-shear rotor-stator homogenization is designed for efficient laboratory sample preparation using mechanical and hydraulic shear rather than ultrasonic cavitation.
Versatile sample processing supports tissue disruption, cell lysis, emulsification, dispersion, mixing, and particle size reduction using the same rotor-stator principle.
A 144W high-torque motor provides variable speed operation from 5,000 to 35,000 rpm for controlled processing across different sample types.
A wide sample volume range processes samples from 0.03 mL to 500 mL as standard, with some probe and viscosity combinations supporting volumes up to 1 L.
One-handed operation comes from thumb-operated variable speed control and an ergonomic housing, making the PRO200 easy to operate with one hand during routine sample preparation.
The PRO Quick Connect probe system lets stainless steel probes be changed quickly while maintaining a secure connection and helping reduce vibration during operation.
Simplified cleaning between samples comes from the quick-connect probe system, making probe changes and cleanup more convenient when processing multiple samples.
Existing PRO Quick Connect probes remain compatible with the redesigned motor, allowing laboratories to upgrade without replacing their current probe collection.

sections.eyebrow: Rotor-Stator Shear Mechanism and Quick Connect Probes
sections.title: Rotor-Stator Shear Mechanism and Quick Connect Probes
sections.description: Understanding how rotor-stator homogenization actually works explains why it handles certain samples differently than an ultrasonic probe would. The generator probe draws material directly into itself, where it passes through the narrow gap between a rotating rotor and a fixed stator, experiencing both mechanical shear from the blade action and hydraulic shear from the turbulent flow that gap creates. The PRO Quick Connect probe system is what makes switching between applications practical rather than a maintenance chore. Coupling stays secure during operation, vibration drops compared to less precise connection systems, and cleaning between samples is straightforward since the stainless-steel probe disconnects cleanly.

sections.title: Configuration Options and Long-Term Support
body: Hand-held operation covers most routine work, but a PRO200 Stand Assembly turns the same motor into a stable, hands-free bench-top setup when that's what a protocol calls for. Complete homogenizing packages bundle the motor unit, generator probe, stand assembly, and accessories together for labs starting from scratch.

Worth knowing if your lab already runs an earlier-generation Bio-Gen PRO200: factory technical assistance, repair services, replacement parts, compatibility guidance, and upgrade support continue for legacy units wherever possible, and because the redesigned motor stays compatible with existing Quick Connect probes, upgrading often doesn't mean replacing everything at once.

faqs.question: What sample volumes can PRO250 handle?

sections.eyebrow: Power, Volume Range, and Repeatable Speed Control
sections.title: Power, Volume Range, and Repeatable Speed Control
sections.description: More power on its own doesn't guarantee repeatable results, it just processes faster. The separate ON/OFF switch is what actually delivers repeatability here: dial in your speed once, and every subsequent run starts at exactly that same setting, since switching off between samples doesn't reset the dial. That power translates directly into volume headroom. 0.03mL to 5L is a genuinely wide range for one hand-held unit, and the 5×75mm to 30×200mm probe range gives you the physical reach to match probe size to sample volume rather than forcing every job through one probe geometry.
